title.value: PETRA: PARALLEL END-TO-END TRAINING OF REVERSIBLE ARCHITECTURES
title.justification: The title of the paper is clearly stated at the beginning of the document as "PETRA: PARALLEL END-TO-END TRAINING OF REVERSIBLE ARCHITECTURES."
title.quote:
Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2025

PETRA: PARALLEL END-TO-END TRAINING OF REVERSIBLE ARCHITECTURES

analysis.description: This paper introduces PETRA, a novel training technique for reversible architectures, aimed at addressing the challenges associated with parallelizing deep model training. PETRA allows gradient computations to be parallelized, optimizing for memory efficiency and minimizing communication overhead. The technique is tested on datasets like CIFAR-10, ImageNet32, and ImageNet, and is found to provide comparable accuracies to backpropagation while utilizing models like ResNet-18, ResNet-34, and ResNet-50.

type.justification: The paper describes and tests a new method (PETRA) for training deep models, specifically reversible architectures. It includes numerical experiments and comparisons of PETRA with backpropagation on various datasets, demonstrating its practical application and effectiveness, which classifies the study as empirical.
type.quote: We develop a custom autograd-like training framework for PETRA, and we demonstrate its effectiveness on CIFAR-10, ImageNet32, and ImageNet, achieving competitive accuracies comparable to backpropagation using ResNet-18, ResNet-34, and ResNet-50 models.

name.justification: The paper focuses on improving techniques for training deep learning models, specifically addressing challenges in parallelizing training through reversible architectures and comparing them with existing models like ResNets.
name.quote: Reversible architectures have been shown to be capable of performing on par with their non-reversible architectures, being applied in deep learning for memory savings and generative modeling.

name.justification: The paper addresses the parallelization of deep learning training and introduces the PETRA method to execute gradient computations in parallel across different stages of the model.
name.quote: PETRA facilitates effective model parallelism by enabling stages (i.e., a set of layers) to compute independently on different devices, while only needing to communicate activations and gradients between each other.

name.justification: The central focus of the paper is on reversible architectures that allow for memory savings and efficient gradient computation during training.
name.quote: We introduce PETRA, a novel method designed to parallelize gradient computations within reversible architectures with minimal computational overhead.

name.justification: ResNet-18 is one of the models used for evaluating the PETRA method, and it is explicitly mentioned in the paper.

is_contributed.justification: ResNet-18 itself is not contributed by this paper, as it is an existing architecture used for comparison.
is_contributed.quote: ...comparable to backpropagation using ResNet-18, ResNet-34, and ResNet-50 models.

is_executed.justification: ResNet-18 is executed using the PETRA method to test its efficacy, as mentioned in the numerical experiments section.
is_executed.quote: We validate the efficacy of PETRA through rigorous testing on benchmark datasets such as CIFAR-10, ImageNet-32, and ImageNet... using ResNet-18, ResNet-34, and ResNet-50 models.

is_compared.justification: ResNet-18 is used as a benchmark to compare the performance of the PETRA method against standard backpropagation.
is_compared.quote: ...achieving competitive accuracies comparable to backpropagation using ResNet-18, ResNet-34, and ResNet-50 models.
